prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Lift ev’ry voice and sing, Till earth and heaven ring, Ring with the harmonies of Liberty; Let our rejoicing rise High as the list’ning skies, Let it resound loud as the rolling sea. Sing a song full of the faith that the dark past has taught us, Sing a song full of the hope that the present has brought us; Facing the rising sun of our new day begun, Let us march on till victory is won. Stony the road we trod, Bitter the chast’ning rod, Felt in the days when hope unborn had died; Yet with a steady beat, Have not our weary feet Come to the place for which our fathers sighed? We have come over a way that with tears has been watered, We have come, treading our path through the blood of the slaughtered, Out from the gloomy past, Till now we stand at last Where the white gleam of our bright star is cast. God of our weary years, God of our silent tears, Thou who has brought us thus far on the way; Thou who has by Thy might, Led us into the light, Keep us forever in the path, we pray. Lest our feet stray from the places, our God, where we met Thee, Lest our hearts, drunk with the wine of the world, we forget Thee; Shadowed beneath Thy hand, May we forever stand. True to our God, True to our native land.

outputs.L2:
Raise every voice in music until the sound fills both sky and earth with freedom’s melody. May our joy climb to the attentive heavens and thunder with the power of the ocean. Let us sing of the trust we gained through former suffering and of the promise offered by the present. With a new era dawning before us, we will continue forward until triumph is achieved.

Our journey crossed harsh ground, and we endured severe punishment during a time when hope seemed unable even to be born. Still, despite exhaustion, our determined steps have carried us to the destination our ancestors longed to reach. We traveled roads soaked with sorrow and tears, advancing where those who were killed had shed their blood. Emerging from a shadowed history, we now finally stand within the shining light of our guiding star.

God who has witnessed our years of weariness and our unspoken grief, You have sustained us throughout this journey. By Your strength, You guided us from darkness into brightness; we ask You to keep us always on the right course. Do not allow us to wander away from the sacred places where we encountered You, or to become so intoxicated by worldly pleasures that we lose all memory of You. May we remain forever sheltered beneath Your protection, faithful both to our God and to the country of our birth.
outputs.L3: The song calls upon every voice to rise in joyful celebration of liberty, joining together in unity and shared purpose. It encourages people to draw strength and faith from the suffering of the past while looking forward with hope to the promise of a new day. At the same time, it remembers the long and bitter journey endured by earlier generations in their struggle for freedom. It honors those whose tears, sacrifices, and blood helped lead their people out of oppression and toward a brighter future. Finally, the song offers a prayer for divine guidance, asking that the people remain steadfast, faithful to God, and devoted to their native land.
outputs.L4:
The hymn recounts the African American journey from bondage and oppression toward freedom, justice, and hope. It begins with a call for all voices to rise together in song, celebrating liberty with a harmony strong enough to reach heaven. Yet its joy is grounded in historical memory: the community has traveled a difficult road, endured bitter suffering, and crossed a path marked by the pain and sacrifice of those who came before. Despite these hardships, faith, courage, and perseverance have carried the people forward into the promise of a brighter day.

The hymn also offers a prayer of gratitude and continued dependence on God. It acknowledges divine guidance through struggle and asks that the community remain faithful, united, and true to its moral and spiritual calling. Even after progress has been made, the danger of forgetting past sacrifices or straying from the path of justice remains. The hymn therefore urges steadfast commitment—to God, to one another, and to the nation—until liberty and equality are fully realized. Blending remembrance, celebration, and prayer, it presents freedom not merely as an achievement of the past, but as an ongoing responsibility sustained by collective resolve and hope.
